'''Suba''' was a [[human]] [[Gender|male]] [[lieutenant]] in the [[Imperial Navy]] who served as [[Chief of Security]] on board the ''[[Executor]]'', [[flagship]] of the [[Sith Lord]] [[Anakin Skywalker|Darth Vader]] and the head of the [[Death Squadron]] [[fleet]]. In [[3 ABY]], Suba was present with [[Admiral]] [[Firmus Piett]] when Vader [[Death|executed]] [[Captain]] [[Lorth Needa]] for losing the rebel [[freighter]] known as the ''[[Millennium Falcon]]'' after the [[Battle of Hoth]].

Vader then ordered Death Squadron to calculate all possible destinations which the ''Falcon'' could have escaped too. The Empire later tracked the ''Falcon'' to the [[planet]] [[Bespin]], and Suba stood on the [[bridge]] while the ''Executor's'' [[tractor beam]] was prepared to capture the vessel. The ''Falcon'' however managed to escape into [[hyperspace]].

==Biography==
Suba<ref name="SWFC">{{ForceCollection|Lieutenant Suba|star=1}}</ref> was a [[human]] [[Gender|male]] who served in the [[Imperial Navy]] and [[Imperial Officer Corps]] of the [[Galactic Empire]].<ref name="ESB" /> By [[3 ABY]],<ref name="Date">''[[Star Wars: Galactic Atlas]]'' dates the events of [[Star Wars: Episode V The Empire Strikes Back|''Star Wars'': Episode V ''The Empire Strikes Back'']], which includes the appearances of Suba, to [[3 ABY]].</ref> Suba held the rank of [[lieutenant]] and worked as the [[Chief of Security]] on board<ref name="SWFC" /> the [[Executor-class Star Dreadnought|''Executor''-class Star Dreadnought]] ''[[Executor]]'', [[flagship]] of the [[Sith Lord]] [[Anakin Skywalker|Darth Vader]] and head of his [[fleet]], [[Death Squadron]].<ref name="OTFL">''[[Star Wars: On the Front Lines]]''</ref> The ''Executor'' took part in [[Project Swarm]],<ref name="Aphra">[[Doctor Aphra (2016) 37|''Doctor Aphra'' (2016) 37]]</ref> a hunt for the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic]]'s [[Echo Base|secret base]], which culminated in Death Squadron [[Blockade|blockading]] the [[planet]] [[Hoth]].<ref name="ESB" />

[[File:Piett_and_Suba.png|thumb|left|250px|Suba served with Piett on the ''Executor''.]]
Following the [[Battle of Hoth]], Vader had the fleet pursue the escaping rebel [[freighter]] known as the ''[[Millennium Falcon]]'', as it was known to carry allies of the [[rebel pilot]] [[Luke Skywalker]]. After the ''Falcon'' was lost from Imperial [[sensor]]s, [[Captain]] [[Lorth Needa]] came to the ''Executor'' to personally apologize for the failure. Suba stood with [[Admiral]] [[Firmus Piett]] at a bank of monitors in one of the ''Executor's'' corridors while Vader [[Telekinesis|choked]] Needa to [[death]] behind the pair. While [[Imperial Navy Trooper|naval troopers]] dragged Needa's corpse away, Piett and Suba turned to Vader and the admiral confirmed that there was no trace of the ''Falcon''.<ref name="ESB" />

Vader gave the order for all possible destinations for the ''Falcon'' to be calculated based on the ship's last known trajectory, warning Piett not to fail him again. Vader then left as Piett ordered Suba and the other officers around him to deploy the fleet, prompting Suba and the others to depart. Ultimately Vader and the Empire tracked down the ''Falcon'' on the planet [[Bespin]], where they captured its [[captain]], [[Han Solo]]. The rest of the freighter's crew managed to escape from the [[city]] in the ''Falcon'', and Suba was on board the ''Executor's'' [[bridge]] as Piett gave the order to prepare the [[Star Destroyer]]'s [[tractor beam]] to capture the rebel ship. However, the ''Falcon'' was able to jump to [[hyperspace]] before they could capture it, escaping the Empire once again.<ref name="ESB" />

An image of Suba standing beside Piett was included in a briefing report sent to the Imperial [[capital]] [[Coruscant]]. The [[historian]] [[Beaumont Kin]] later included the image in his [[book]] ''[[The Rise and Fall of the Galactic Empire]]''<ref name="Rise">''[[Star Wars: The Rise and Fall of the Galactic Empire]]''</ref> in [[35 ABY]].<ref name="RiseDate">{{RiseAndFallDate}}</ref>

==Personality and traits==
Suba did not approve of Vader's obsession with capturing Skywalker, but never objected to the Sith Lord's orders.<ref name="SWFC" /> He had fair skin, [[Color|blue]] [[eye]]s and brown [[hair]].<ref name="ESB" />

==Equipment==
Suba wore the olive-gray [[Imperial officer's uniform|uniform]] of an Imperial naval officer, including one [[code cylinder]], a [[rank insignia plaque]] with two red bars above two blue, and a [[Imperial kepi|cap]].<ref name="ESB" />

==Behind the scenes==
Suba first appeared [[1980]] [[original trilogy]] film, [[Star Wars: Episode V The Empire Strikes Back|''Star Wars'': Episode V ''The Empire Strikes Back'']]. In Suba's final scene in the film, he and Piett's rank badges originally appeared on the wrong side of their uniforms,<ref name="ESB" /> but this was corrected in the [[2004]] DVD release of the film.<ref name="DVD">{{SWArchive|url=episode-v/release/video/f20060901/index.html|text=Episode V: What Has Changed?}}</ref> In the new ''[[Star Wars]]'' [[canon]], Suba was first used in the [[Star Wars video games|mobile card game]] ''[[Star Wars: Force Collection]]'',<ref name="SWFC" /> which initially launched in [[2013]]. Although the launch of ''Force Collection'' predates<ref name="Force Collection release">{{SW|url=news/announcing-star-wars-force-collection|text=Announcing Star Wars: Force Collection|nolive=1}}</ref> the ''Star Wars'' canon reset of [[2014]],<ref name="Legends">{{SW|url=news/the-legendary-star-wars-expanded-universe-turns-a-new-page|text=The Legendary Star Wars Expanded Universe Turns a New Page}}</ref> [[Lucasfilm Story Group]] member [[Leland Chee]] confirmed that the game was kept updated to fit with canon.<ref name="Twitter">{{Twitter|holocronkeeper|status/846807700482666496|[[Leland Chee]]|quote=I'm not gonna go through the trouble of changing them and I don't have any reason to believe currently that anyone would. […] On the off-chance that we DID have a current need to change any of these, we would have for Force Collection.|archivefile=File:Leland_Chee_Force_Collection.png}} — [[Leland Chee]] of the [[Lucasfilm Story Group]] has confirmed that [[in-universe]] information from ''[[Star Wars: Force Collection]]'' conforms with ''[[Star Wars]]'' [[canon]].</ref> The name originated in the [[Star Wars Legends|''Star Wars'' Legends]] continuity, where it was first used on a card in the [[1997]] [[Dagobah Limited]] set for the [[Star Wars Customizable Card Game|''Star Wars'' Customizable Card Game]].<ref name="Dagobah">{{CCG|set=Dagobah Limited|cardname=Lieutenant Suba}}</ref>
